title: Surface 95th/99th tail latency per route/model/region and integrate with loadbench
creator: Lena Park
description:
Goal: Build an end-to-end path to collect, store, visualize, and alert on 95th and 99th percentile (tail) latency broken down by route, model, and region, and wire those signals into the existing loadbench regression detection pipeline. This ticket scopes the telemetry schema changes, aggregation pipeline, dashboard surfaces, and a staged rollout plan that minimizes ingestion cost while preserving signal fidelity for regressions.

Why now: customer incidents and internal benchmarks show sporadic tail spikes undetected by mean/median metrics. We need sliceable, comparable tail signals to tie regressions back to model variants, region routing, or request patterns. Integrating with loadbench will allow automated regression gate checks during CI and monthly perf sweeps.

Non-goals: per-request flamegraphs or detailed per-kernel timings (covered in separate runtime profiling work).
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented request path emits slice keys: route, model_version, region, client_tier at request start and token-stream end
Aggregation pipeline computes rolling 95th and 99th percentiles with 1m windows and 1h retention rollups per slice
New dashboards in Console: Tail Latency Explorer with pivoting by route/model/region and an exportable CSV
Bench harness (loadbench) can assert no >20% regression in p95/p99 vs baseline for a given route-model-region during nightly runs
Alerting: automated PagerDuty alerts when p99 exceeds configured threshold for a customer-impacting route for >3 consecutive minutes
Documentation: runbook + rollout notes and a Confluence page describing signal semantics and recommended SLA thresholds
tasks: Design telemetry schema: add 'slice_key' set (route,model,region,client_tier) and event types for 'request.start' and 'request.complete'
Implement low-overhead histogram summarizer in edge SDK to emit quantile sketches (t-digest) for 1m buckets
Extend aggregation pipeline to ingest sketches and compute exact p95/p99 via merge; store results in time-series DB and S3 rollups
Create Console dashboard panels and a filterable explorer view; add CSV/JSON export and pre-sliced links for common queries
Add regression detector rule in loadbench: baseline ingestion + statistical significance test (bootstrap) for p95/p99
Write alerts and playbook: severity levels, noise suppression, automatic reroute suggestions, and oncall runbook
Staged rollout: internal -> staging clusters -> 10% of prod -> 100%; monitor cost and cardinality growth at each step
comments: 2025-09-11 - Lena Park: Initial design posted to Confluence (link below). Proposing t-digest on the edge summarizer to avoid per-token traffic. Open questions on cardinality budget for 'model_version' — recommend bucketing minor patch versions.

2025-09-12 - Dmitri Volkov: Prototype of edge summarizer implemented. Microbench shows ~0.8% p95 difference vs full-stream measurement for 1m windows. Putting PR up: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521
2025-09-14 - Sasha Rivera (observability): Suggested adding 'client_tier' to slice keys to help separate free-tier noise. Also flagged need for retention tiering to S3 rollups to keep costs bounded.

2025-09-15 - Dmitri Volkov: Aggregation pipeline sketch merge job implemented and tested against historical replay dataset (see results dashboard). Observed 12% increase in storage at 1m granularity; adding hourly rollups to mitigate.
2025-09-16 - PM review by Raj Patel: Approved thresholds and customer-impact classifications. Requested an exportable CSV API for SRE postmortems.
2025-09-18 - QA: Loadbench integration tests added. Nightly regression job passes on staging; one false positive found due to traffic shaping in replay harness (investigating).
